title: Manufacture of Concentrated, Lipid-based Oxygen Microbubble Emulsions by High Shear Homogenization and Serial Concentration
protocol: Place a sterilized, wide-mouthed 4 L glass collection vessel beneath the single stage mixer.
Ensure a gas-tight fitting between the mixer head and the mouth of the vessel using rubber seals or tape.
Fit one base port of the HCT with sterile tubing approximately 10 inches long, fitted with a 3-way stopcock at the tip for collecting concentrated emulsion.
Fit the second base port of the HCT with sterile tubing approximately 36 inches in length.
Feed the 36-inch tubing through a roller pump.
Connect tubing from the second base port, through the roller pump to one side port of a T-piece.
Attach the other side port of the T-piece to an oxygen tank using a low-flow gas flowmeter.
Fit the inlet of the high shear homogenizer with the T-piece including two ports.
Connect the outlet port of the high shear homogenizer to the inlet port of an in-line heat exchanger maintained at 4 °C.
Connect the outlet port of the heat exchanger to the return port of the HCT, creating a closed loop system.
Attach an oxygen tank via a flowmeter to the HCT port #4.
Attach a gas composition monitor that is open to atmosphere to the top port of the HCT (port #5).
Sterilize glass and metal components by autoclave if sterility is desired before each use.
Sterilize tubing components and plastic connectors by ethylene oxide before each use.
Place 20 g of DSPC and 10 g of cholesterol in the base of the HCT.
Add 1 L of Plasma-Lyte A to the HCT and hand stir for 1 min, integrating lipid into aqueous phase.
Lower the single stage mixer into the aqueous phase, ensuring it is fully covered by the aqueous phase.
Ensure the top of the HCT is gas tight with no open side ports.
Turn on the gas source attached to port #4 until oxygen fraction in headspace reaches >95%.
Mix precursor emulsion for 5 min at 5,000 rpm using the single stage mixer.
Store unused lipid-water mixture at 4 ºC for up to 30 days before use.
Prime the entire closed loop system with the precursor emulsion by turning on the roller pump at 1.3 LPM.
Keep the roller pump on at 1.3 LPM.
Turn on the in-line high shear homogenizer to 7,500 rpm.
Immediately thereafter, turn on oxygen flow to the inlet portion of the homogenizer at 0.5 LPM.
Keep the single stage mixer (in the HCT) on at 3,500 rpm.
Titrate down gas flow until fluid is opaque and contains no visible gas bubbles if air bubbles are present in the tubing exiting the mixer.
Run the system for 15 min.
Turn off the high shear homogenizer.
Turn off the oxygen inlet to the high shear homogenizer.
Continue to run the single stage mixer in the HCT until the emulsion is removed.
Attach a sterile, modified 140 ml luer-lock syringe to the stopcock attached to base port #1 on the collection vessel.
Draw up 100 ml of fluid using the syringe.
Tightly cap the syringe and repeat until all fluid has been removed.
Withdraw 100 ml of air into each syringe and saw off excess plunger and syringe material above the 140 ml mark.
Fill and empty modified syringes using toothed forceps to draw up the plunger.
Centrifuge modified syringes with the capped end oriented downward in a refrigerated (4 ºC) bucket centrifuge at 225 x g for 10 min.
Expel the bottom layer of excess cloudy aqueous phase and discard it.
Transfer concentrated foam, which is contained in the second bright white layer, to a gas-impermeable syringe using a three-way stopcock to prevent ambient gas contamination.
Discard the final layer containing free oxygen gas from ruptured LOMs.
Assess foam quality by reaching ≥90% gas in concentrated foam.
Calculate gas concentration using the formula: Volume % gas = [(Foam weight / Foam volume) - 1] x 100.
Size microbubbles by light obscuration to determine if particle size is within the expected range.
Tightly cap the glass syringe with a luer-lock fitting.
